notes.verdict: H3 (mirror reserve) is supported and H1 (RAM residency after the GPU prefill) is not. GB is slower than GR on the identical long text (median 2.5778 vs 2.6355 tok/s, -2.2%) and on the identical short text (2.6649 vs 2.7326, -2.5%). The extra time is in attach: GB uploads +1909 experts (long) and +2035 (short) more, at the same ~1.1 ms per upload. fetch_wait is lower in GB than in GR (-0.40 s long, -0.37 s short), not higher. The VRAM plateau is 2236 MiB lower in GB (about 175 fewer 12.75 MiB mirrors, 1096 vs 1271). On the identical short text, GR is within 0.4% of CU (+0.244 s over 199 tokens; uploads +51, fetch_wait +0.11 s). So the prefill path itself costs about nothing once the reserve is equal. On the long text GR-CU is +1.88 s (+9.5 ms/token: attach +1.30 s from +1172 uploads, fetch_wait +0.57 s). That comparison is between DIFFERENT token sequences: the CPU-union prefill picks a different first token ('This' vs 'The'). Both mirror caches start empty and have the same capacity, so the upload difference comes from the different routing. Only the fetch_wait part, at most 0.57 s (about 2.9 ms/token, under 1%), could be RAM residency. The shape does not match H1 either. The GR-CU gap is not front-loaded (+0.32 s in the first 24 intervals, then -0.5 to +2.4 s swings in tokens 25-150) and is mostly uploads. The GB-GR reserve gap is not front-loaded either. Without the cold GB s1 it is +0.8 ms/token in tokens 1-10, while the mirror cache is still filling (about 5 s to its plateau), and then a steady +5 to +10 ms/token from token 11 on (mean +8.6 ms/token over tokens 25-199). That is the shape of a capacity limit. Only GB s1, the first and coldest sample, adds a front-loaded +16 ms/token over tokens 1-24. The only front-loaded component anywhere is GR-CU on the short text: +0.20 s in its first 24 intervals and about 0 after that (fetch_wait +0.11 s, uploads +51). That is the largest possible residency transient, about 0.3% of the answer.
notes.text_divergence: long_200 texts: GB and GR are byte-identical (sha 59c44faffdb46066) in all 6 samples, and CU is self-consistent in all 3 (sha 6382d935628488d2). But CU differs from GB/GR from the first token: 'This text is a highly repetitive, struct...' vs 'The text is a highly repetitive, structu...'. Each arm is deterministic, so this is not a race. The CPU-union prefill (MoE on the CPU, expert_matmul_s 135.7 s) and the GPU-bank prefill (MoE on the GPU) are different kernels. Their final hidden state differs by rounding, and that flips a near-tie on this prompt's first token. docs/deepseek-v4.md at d0e19de2 says as much: different kernels are not bit-identical in general. But the PR #1 docs line 'Answers were identical to the CPU union in every run' holds only for the two benchmark prompts. short_200 is byte-identical in all 9 samples.
notes.original_f42: Original F42 observation (manifests/final/pr1, 2026-10-15): dev (arm A, COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH=1 set but the bank refused for REAP) vs the pr1 tip (arm B). Its GPU0 decode plateau on request 1 was 22064 MiB for dev vs 21262 MiB for pr1 (A/s2, B/s2 nvsmi.csv), about 63 more mirrors for dev. That reserve gap is about a third of the GB-vs-GR gap here (175 mirrors). So the reserve explains part of the original 24-token gap (2.054 vs 2.247 chunks/s, about 1.0 s over 24 tokens), but not all of it. In this run the first 24 intervals of long_200 differ GB(s2,s3)-GR +0.13 s and GR-CU +0.32 s, on different texts for GR-CU. The original texts were identical but the prompt's closing question was different (24-token answer), so this run does not reproduce that window like for like.
notes.cache_state: GB s1 (the first sample of the window, serve-unit memory peak 14.6G) is the slow outlier of GB: long fetch_wait 15.39 s vs 14.32/14.40 s and dec_moe total 49.21 vs 47.71/47.72 s. Medians and the 'mean_GB_s1_excluded' decomposition are robust to it, and round 3 alone (memory peaks 7.9-8.0G) gives the same picture.
notes.uploads_deterministic: uploads per request are identical in all 3 samples of each arm (long 18806/15725/16897, short 20189/18103/18154 for GB/CU/GR). They are a deterministic function of routing and mirror capacity, and attach costs the same 1.13 ms (long) / 1.07 ms (short) per upload in every arm (12.75 MiB at ~11 GB/s, PCIe 4.0 x8).
